findings.description: The 'data' bucket sets no ACL/public access block and is documented as public, so objects such as the customer master file can be read by anyone on the internet. No aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block is defined to prevent public ACLs or policies.
No server_side_encryption_configuration is defined, so sensitive customer data is stored without enforced encryption at rest and without a customer-managed KMS key.
The bucket has no logging block, so reads and writes to publicly exposed customer data leave no S3 access audit trail.
Versioning is not enabled, so object overwrite or deletion (including malicious or ransomware-driven deletion) is unrecoverable and tamper-evidence is lost.
A customer master spreadsheet is uploaded into the publicly accessible, unencrypted 'data' bucket, directly exposing sensitive customer records.
The financials bucket has no server_side_encryption_configuration, leaving financial data unencrypted at rest.
No logging block is configured, so access to financial data is not auditable.
Versioning is not enabled, so deletion or tampering of financial objects cannot be detected or recovered.
No aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block is associated with this bucket, so a later public ACL or bucket policy would take effect unimpeded.
No server_side_encryption_configuration is defined for the operations bucket, so its data is stored unencrypted.
The operations bucket has no logging block, leaving no audit trail of object access.
No public access block is configured, so public ACLs or policies applied later would not be blocked at the account/bucket level.
The data science bucket lacks server_side_encryption_configuration, so its contents are not encrypted at rest with a managed key.
No aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block guards this bucket against subsequently applied public ACLs or bucket policies.
The log bucket has no public access block; log data containing access patterns and identifiers could be exposed if a public ACL or policy is later applied.
The central log bucket does not itself have access logging enabled, so tampering with or reading of audit logs is not recorded.
No bucket policy denies non-HTTPS requests (aws:SecureTransport = false), so data can be transferred to and from these buckets in cleartext.
